title: The Bhaktirasamritasindhu
altTitles: Ocean of the Nectar of Devotion
author: rupa-gosvamin
attributionNote: Written by Rupa Gosvamin at Vrindavan, one of the six Gosvamins who systematised the teaching of Chaitanya. His own commentary, the Durgamasangamani, accompanies the verses.
description: The Bhaktirasamritasindhu is the systematic theology of devotion in the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition: it defines devotion and its varieties, sets out the practices that lead to it, analyses the emotional states and the stages through which love of Krishna matures, and ranks the different forms that love takes — concluding that the love of the cowherd women of Vrindavan, and of Radha above all, is the highest.
historicalContext: The work turned the devotional movement around Chaitanya into a school with a theology, and its vocabulary for the emotions of love became the common property of later Vaishnava writing in Bengal and Braj.
availabilityNote: Complete: the Sanskrit verses of all four divisions as GRETIL publishes them, streamed from GRETIL at read time, one chapter at a time. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation.
